Pipeline

Where the data comes from.

Most financial-news APIs hand you a firehose and wish you luck. We filter before a story ever costs you a request, so what reaches the API is the part worth a model's context window.

01

Collect

A GDELT-driven monitor watches the global financial press around the clock, while a second worker tails SEC EDGAR for Form 4 and 8-K filings. Hand-curated publisher RSS feeds fill the gaps neither catches. Everything lands in one feed.

02

Enrich

An LLM pass scores each article 1–10 for relevance, assigns it a topic category, and writes per-ticker sentiment with a confidence level and reasoning.

03

Validate

Extracted tickers are checked against the active-symbol list and the article text itself. Hallucinated symbols get dropped, PR-wire spam domains are blocked outright, and near-duplicates collapse into one row.

04

Serve

Only articles that clear the relevance floor and carry at least one verified ticker reach the API. Fewer than 1 in 5 makes the cut, from 6,900+ monitored sources, so the noise never reaches your parser.

Endpoints

stable

GET/api/news/

The feed, newest first, cursor-paginated (10 per page by default; page_size= takes any value from 1 to 20, or up to 50 on a Pro key — pass next_cursor back as cursor=). Filters: symbol, category (CSV or repeated), exclude_categories, min_relevance. Add collapse=story to return one row per story instead of every syndicated reprint, with story_id, sources_count and sources on each item. For polling, add sort=ingested: rows arrive in the order they entered the feed, next_cursor is always returned, and an empty page means you are caught up.

GET/api/news/trending/

Top stories from the last 48h: relevance score ≥ 8, ranked by score decayed by article age so fresh stories lead, at most two stories per ticker. Syndicated reprints of one story are collapsed to a single representative, and each item carries story_id, sources_count and sources for the story it represents.

GET/api/news/insider/

SEC Form 4 insider-transaction feed. Each item carries a structured insider block: trade side, shares, average price, total value, 10b5-1 flag, the reporting owner, and when the filing landed (filed_at, plus late_filing for the ones that missed the two business day deadline). Same shape and cursor pagination as the main feed (10 per page by default; page_size= 1-20, or up to 50 on Pro); symbol= to scope, min_relevance= to keep only larger trades. For polling, add sort=ingested, the same delta mode the main feed offers. A Form 4 is filed days after the trade it reports, so a new event often enters the feed below the newest page and a poller reading only the head will miss it.

GET/api/news/{uid}/

Fetch a single article by UID with full enrichment (per-ticker analysis, category, key entities).

GET/api/news/{uid}/related/

Up to 6 related articles — fresh shared-ticker stories first, then same-category backfill.

GET/api/symbols/

List supported tickers with metadata (name, sector, exchange, country, currency), alphabetical. Full list by default (~10k); optional limit= / offset= to slice, or search= to resolve a name or ticker prefix (search=bitcoin returns BTC-USD).

GET/api/symbols/{ticker}/

Fetch a single symbol with extended metadata. Resolves delisted symbols too: check status, and renamed_to for the successor ticker when the company continues under a new symbol. News queries for a renamed ticker include articles tagged with the former one, and any share class of an issuer includes articles tagged with its other listed classes (GOOGL includes rows tagged GOOG).

GET/api/symbols/{ticker}/sentiment-summary/

7-day AI sentiment rollup for one ticker: bullish / neutral / bearish counts plus per-day buckets.

GET/api/symbols/{ticker}/insider-summary/

30-day insider activity from Form 4: buy/sell counts, dollar volumes, % under 10b5-1 plans, most active insiders.

Authenticate with Authorization: Bearer ak_live_…. Quotas have two layers, a per-minute burst cap and a per-day volume cap, both counted against your account rather than per key. Free is for evaluation and non-commercial use; production needs a paid plan. The same key also authenticates the MCP server for headless agents (send it as a Bearer header there too); interactive AI clients connect to MCP over OAuth instead.

GET /api/news/?sort=ingesteddelta polling

Articles reach the feed later than their publish time: general news lands a median of ~33 minutes after publication, SEC filings in 5 to 9 minutes (measured 2026-07-25). A poller that tracks time_published therefore misses late arrivals. sort=ingested returns rows in the order they entered the feed instead: call once without a cursor, store the next_cursor, then repeat the call with it. In this mode every response carries a cursor, and an empty results list means you are caught up. All filters work unchanged. Responses are cached for 60 seconds, so polling more often than once a minute buys nothing. Keep passing sort=ingested on every call: each mode issues its own cursors, and replaying one into the other mode returns a 400 rather than silently restarting at the top of the feed. The same mode works on /api/news/insider/, where the gap is widest: a Form 4 is filed days after the trade it reports, so a new event often enters the feed already below the newest page.

# pip install alphai-sdk
import time

from alphai import Client

cursor = None  # persist this between runs

with Client() as client:  # reads $ALPHAI_API_KEY
    while True:
        page = client.news.list(sort="ingested", cursor=cursor)
        for article in page.results:
            print(f"[{article.relevance_score}/10] {article.title}")
        cursor = page.next_cursor  # always present in this mode
        time.sleep(900)  # 96 polls/day fits the Free daily cap

That is the official Python SDK doing the cursor bookkeeping. There is a TypeScript one with the same sort option, and the endpoint stays a plain GET if you would rather carry no dependency.

Understanding the data

What the fields mean.

Every news item ships an enrichment block produced by an LLM pass over the article. These are the four fields you'll use most.

Scores rate the article, not the company it mentions: a recap of a mega-cap's week-old earnings scores low, while a small-cap's fresh FDA approval scores high. Scoring is deterministic: the same article always gets the same score, and SEC Form 4 filings are scored from the transaction itself (size, buy vs. sell, 10b5-1 plan or not) rather than by the model.

Need the formal contract? The interactive API reference lives at /api/schema/swagger-ui/ (Swagger UI, with the raw OpenAPI spec linked at the top).

enrichment.relevance_scoreint 1–10

How much trading value the article itself carries.

  • 1–2 · no trading relevance — lifestyle, solicitations, short-interest scrapes.
  • 3–4 · derivative content about already-known events — opinion pieces, recaps, 13F stake writeups, market wraps.
  • 5–6 · macro/sector datapoints with read-across; minor-but-real company news.
  • 7–8 · real company news — analyst actions with a thesis, settlements, clinical data, same-day moves with a fresh catalyst.
  • 9–10 · primary, material, newly disclosed — M&A, prints with numbers, approvals, major contracts.

The /api/news/ feed defaults to ≥ 4; pass ?min_relevance=N to relax or tighten the filter.

enrichment.ai_trading_insights.ticker_analysis[].impact_analysis.sentimentenum

Per-ticker price impact direction. Not earnings-positive vs earnings-negative — this is "where will the chart move on this story."

  • positive — bullish
  • neutral — sideways
  • negative — bearish

Each ticker block also carries impact_analysis.confidence (high / medium / low) and a free-text reasoning field, which helps when you filter an automation pipeline down to confident bullish or bearish signals.

enrichment.categoryenum

One topic bucket per article. Use ?category=earnings (CSV or repeated for OR-matching) on /api/news/ to filter the feed, or ?exclude_categories= to drop buckets you never trade on.

earnings3,552mergers_acquisitions859regulation881macro_economy168sector_analysis745market_movers1,463technology1,710commodities65crypto399ipo31geopolitics60insider268corporate_actions930other3,469

The numbers are article counts from the last 7 days of the live feed, refreshed every 15 minutes.

enrichment.tickers + ticker_analysis[].tickerstring[]

Tickers extracted from the article. We only retain symbols that exist in our /api/symbols/ list of active symbols (US equities, cryptocurrencies, and foreign listings), so articles that don't mention any active ticker are filtered out before they reach the API. US equities use the bare symbol, cryptocurrencies use a -USD suffix like BTC-USD, and foreign listings use a Yahoo suffix like VOD.L. Each ticker also gets a dedicated ticker_analysis entry with sentiment and reasoning, so multi-ticker stories don't collapse to a single read.

?collapse=storyparam

One real event reported by N outlets is N rows by default. Add ?collapse=story on /api/news/ to get one row per story instead — the representative article carries story_id (its own UID, resolvable via /api/news/{uid}/), sources_count (how many distinct outlets ran it, usually 1 because most stories are carried by a single outlet), and sources (the distinct domains). These fields are null in the default feed. Filters like symbol and category apply to the representative row, so a story whose representative doesn't match is omitted.

Insider data · SEC EDGAR

Form 4 filings, as news.

A dedicated worker tails SEC EDGAR and turns every Form 4 filing (officer and director buys and sells) into a feed row shortly after it's filed. One row covers one economic event: all of a filing's non-derivative trades of the same type and holding form, aggregated into a single article. The JSON shape matches every other article, so your parser doesn't need a special case.

Form 4 summaries are deterministic templates built from the filing itself: insider name, role, transaction code, total shares, price (volume-weighted average and executed range when a sale runs across tranches), and total value. There is no LLM paraphrase between you and the disclosure. The relevance score is computed from the event itself — its total size, buy vs. sell, 10b5-1 plan or not — so it's reproducible.

  • GET /api/news/insider/ — the Form 4 insider feed, cursor-paginated, ?symbol= to scope.
  • GET /api/news/?category=insider — the same rows through the main feed's category filter.
  • GET /api/symbols/{ticker}/insider-summary/ — 30-day rollup: buys vs. sells, dollar volumes, % under 10b5-1 plans, most active insiders.
  • GET /api/symbols/{ticker}/sentiment-summary/ — its sibling: 7-day bullish / neutral / bearish counts from the news flow.

Webhooks · Pro

Push, not poll.

Register HTTPS endpoints in /account/webhooks and receive a signed POST when a high-relevance news article hits one of your ticker subscriptions. Same article shape as GET /api/news/<uid>/.

  • One delivery per story. When several outlets carry the same event, you get one POST for it, not one per outlet.
  • HMAC-SHA256 signature header (Stripe-style, identical scheme).
  • Retry with exponential backoff (1m → 5m → 30m → 2h → 12h).
  • SSRF guard refuses private and loopback targets.
  • Up to 5 endpoints per Pro account.
  • Auto-disable after 10 consecutive 5xx + email to the owner.

Verify the signature

import hashlib
import hmac

def verify(secret: str, signature_header: str, body: bytes) -> bool:
    """Return True iff X-Alphai-Signature header matches the body."""
    parts = dict(p.split("=", 1) for p in signature_header.split(",") if "=" in p)
    ts, sig = parts.get("t"), parts.get("v1")
    if not ts or not sig:
        return False  # malformed header is a failed check, not an exception
    expected = hmac.new(
        secret.encode(),
        ts.encode() + b"." + body,
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected, sig)

FAQ

Questions, answered.

The short version of what the stock news API is, what the free tier gives you, and how it fits next to a market-data API.

What is the alphai stock news API?

A REST API that serves financial news as plain JSON over HTTPS. Every article arrives already scored for relevance (1–10) and tagged with the tickers it affects, plus per-ticker sentiment and written reasoning. Authenticate with a Bearer key, then filter by symbol, category, or minimum relevance and page the feed with a cursor. The same API powers alphai.io itself.

Is there a free financial news API?

Yes. The Free plan gives you one API key, capped at 20 requests a minute and 100 a day. That's enough to evaluate the feed and build a prototype, and it doesn't ask for a credit card. For production and commercial use, Basic and Pro raise the caps and open more of the archive.

How is this different from a market-data or financial-data API?

Market-data APIs give you prices, fundamentals, and OHLC bars. alphai is a news API. It tells you what happened, which tickers it touches, and how material it is, but it won't quote you a price. Many teams pair it with a market-data API and use the relevance score and sentiment to decide which stories a model or trading bot should act on.

Does the API cover SEC filings and insider trading?

Yes. SEC EDGAR Form 4 insider filings flow through the same feed as press news, in the same JSON shape. Query them with ?category=insider or the dedicated /api/news/insider/ endpoint, and pull a 30-day per-ticker rollup from /api/symbols/{ticker}/insider-summary/. 8-K filings are in there too, categorized by item: earnings releases under ?category=earnings, completed acquisitions under mergers_acquisitions, the rest under corporate_actions.

A poller that tracks time_published therefore misses late arrivals. sort=ingested returns rows in the order they entered the feed instead: call once without a cursor, store the next_cursor, then repeat the call with it. In this mode every response carries a cursor, and an empty results list means you are caught up. All filters work unchanged. Responses are cached for 60 seconds, so polling more often than once a minute buys nothing. Keep passing sort=ingested on every call: each mode issues its own cursors, and replaying one into the other mode returns a 400 rather than silently restarting at the top of the feed. The same mode works on /api/news/insider/, where the gap is widest: a Form 4 is filed days after the trade it reports, so a new event often enters the feed already below the newest page.# pip install alphai-sdk import time from alphai import Client cursor = None # persist this between runs with Client() as client: # reads $ALPHAI_API_KEY while True: page = client.news.list(sort="ingested", cursor=cursor) for article in page.results: print(f"[{article.relevance_score}/10] {article.title}") cursor = page.next_cursor # always present in this mode time.sleep(900) # 96 polls/day fits the Free daily capThat is the official Python SDK doing the cursor bookkeeping. There is a TypeScript one with the same sort option, and the endpoint stays a plain GET if you would rather carry no dependency.Understanding the dataWhat the fields mean.Every news item ships an enrichment block produced by an LLM pass over the article. These are the four fields you'll use most.Scores rate the article, not the company it mentions: a recap of a mega-cap's week-old earnings scores low, while a small-cap's fresh FDA approval scores high. Scoring is deterministic: the same article always gets the same score, and SEC Form 4 filings are scored from the transaction itself (size, buy vs. sell, 10b5-1 plan or not) rather than by the model.Need the formal contract? The interactive API reference lives at /api/schema/swagger-ui/ (Swagger UI, with the raw OpenAPI spec linked at the top).enrichment.relevance_scoreint 1–10How much trading value the article itself carries.1–2 · no trading relevance — lifestyle, solicitations, short-interest scrapes.3–4 · derivative content about already-known events — opinion pieces, recaps, 13F stake writeups, market wraps.5–6 · macro/sector datapoints with read-across; minor-but-real company news.7–8 · real company news — analyst actions with a thesis, settlements, clinical data, same-day moves with a fresh catalyst.9–10 · primary, material, newly disclosed — M&A, prints with numbers, approvals, major contracts.The /api/news/ feed defaults to ≥ 4; pass ?min_relevance=N to relax or tighten the filter.enrichment.ai_trading_insights.ticker_analysis[].impact_analysis.sentimentenumPer-ticker price impact direction. Not earnings-positive vs earnings-negative — this is "where will the chart move on this story."positive — bullishneutral — sidewaysnegative — bearishEach ticker block also carries impact_analysis.confidence (high / medium / low) and a free-text reasoning field, which helps when you filter an automation pipeline down to confident bullish or bearish signals.enrichment.categoryenumOne topic bucket per article. Use ?category=earnings (CSV or repeated for OR-matching) on /api/news/ to filter the feed, or ?exclude_categories= to drop buckets you never trade on.earnings3,552mergers_acquisitions859regulation881macro_economy168sector_analysis745market_movers1,463technology1,710commodities65crypto399ipo31geopolitics60insider268corporate_actions930other3,469The numbers are article counts from the last 7 days of the live feed, refreshed every 15 minutes.enrichment.tickers + ticker_analysis[].tickerstring[]Tickers extracted from the article. We only retain symbols that exist in our /api/symbols/ list of active symbols (US equities, cryptocurrencies, and foreign listings), so articles that don't mention any active ticker are filtered out before they reach the API. US equities use the bare symbol, cryptocurrencies use a -USD suffix like BTC-USD, and foreign listings use a Yahoo suffix like VOD.L. Each ticker also gets a dedicated ticker_analysis entry with sentiment and reasoning, so multi-ticker stories don't collapse to a single read.?collapse=storyparamOne real event reported by N outlets is N rows by default. Add ?collapse=story on /api/news/ to get one row per story instead — the representative article carries story_id (its own UID, resolvable via /api/news/{uid}/), sources_count (how many distinct outlets ran it, usually 1 because most stories are carried by a single outlet), and sources (the distinct domains). These fields are null in the default feed. Filters like symbol and category apply to the representative row, so a story whose representative doesn't match is omitted.Insider data · SEC EDGARForm 4 filings, as news.A dedicated worker tails SEC EDGAR and turns every Form 4 filing (officer and director buys and sells) into a feed row shortly after it's filed. One row covers one economic event: all of a filing's non-derivative trades of the same type and holding form, aggregated into a single article. The JSON shape matches every other article, so your parser doesn't need a special case.Form 4 summaries are deterministic templates built from the filing itself: insider name, role, transaction code, total shares, price (volume-weighted average and executed range when a sale runs across tranches), and total value. There is no LLM paraphrase between you and the disclosure. The relevance score is computed from the event itself — its total size, buy vs. sell, 10b5-1 plan or not — so it's reproducible.GET /api/news/insider/ — the Form 4 insider feed, cursor-paginated, ?symbol= to scope.GET /api/news/?category=insider — the same rows through the main feed's category filter.GET /api/symbols/{ticker}/insider-summary/ — 30-day rollup: buys vs. sells, dollar volumes, % under 10b5-1 plans, most active insiders.GET /api/symbols/{ticker}/sentiment-summary/ — its sibling: 7-day bullish / neutral / bearish counts from the news flow.The insider trading API, in detail →GET /api/symbols/NVDA/insider-summary/{ "ticker": "NVDA", "days": 30, "total_transactions": 14, "buy_count": 2, "sell_count": 12, "buy_value_usd": "1240000.00", "sell_value_usd": "224580213.05", "pct_10b5_1": 64, "top_insiders": [ { "name": "STEVENS MARK A", "title": "Director", "transaction_count": 3, "net_value": "-221102600.00" }, { "name": "Dabiri John", "title": "Director", "transaction_count": 1, "net_value": "-133750.00" } ] }Value fields are decimal strings in USD; buy_value_usd / sell_value_usd are null when the window has no buys or sells. net_value is buys minus sells per insider; title can be empty when the filer reports as a director without an officer role.Workflows people shipWhat an API-connected bot can do.From watchlist alerts to Telegram bots, it's the same JSON in whatever stack you run. The API stays out of your way.PlaygroundTry the API right here.Live responses from the real API, proxied through this site so you don't need a login or a key to explore. Direct calls to api.alphai.io always require an API key — sign up for one and metered headroom.Response// click Send to fetch a live responseRate limitsPriced for scale.Quotas are per account: a per-minute burst cap plus a per-day volume cap. Every keyed response carries X-RateLimit-Limit, -Remaining and -Reset headers, and a 429 adds Retry-After plus your tier's caps and an upgrade pointer in the JSON body. Feed pagination is depth-gated per plan: paging past your archive horizon returns 403 with the same hint; Pro keys page back 180 days. One honest note on the archive: our collectors expanded in June 2026, so months before that hold fewer articles per day than the current feed. Both api.alphai.io and the public /api/news and /api/symbols routes on alphai.io require a key: keyless requests get a 401. To try the API without signing up, use the playground above, which proxies the read-only public endpoints through this site. Send a key for predictable headroom.Full pricing →PlanRate limitArchiveActive keysFree20 / min · 100 / day30 days1Basic60 / min · 10,000 / day90 days1Pro150 / min · 100,000 / day180 days5Webhooks · ProPush, not poll.Register HTTPS endpoints in /account/webhooks and receive a signed POST when a high-relevance news article hits one of your ticker subscriptions. Same article shape as GET /api/news/<uid>/.One delivery per story. When several outlets carry the same event, you get one POST for it, not one per outlet.HMAC-SHA256 signature header (Stripe-style, identical scheme).Retry with exponential backoff (1m → 5m → 30m → 2h → 12h).SSRF guard refuses private and loopback targets.Up to 5 endpoints per Pro account.Auto-disable after 10 consecutive 5xx + email to the owner.Payload — news.matched.v1POST https://your-service.example.com/alphai-webhook Content-Type: application/json User-Agent: alphai-webhook/1.0 X-Alphai-Event: news.matched X-Alphai-Delivery: 42 X-Alphai-Signature: t=1715932000,v1=<hex-HMAC-SHA256> { "id": "evt_42", "type": "news.matched.v1", "created_at": "2026-05-17T07:08:00Z", "delivery_attempt": 1, "data": { "alert": { "ticker": "NVDA" }, "article": { ...same as GET /api/news/<uid>/ } } }Verify the signatureimport hashlib import hmac def verify(secret: str, signature_header: str, body: bytes) -> bool: """Return True iff X-Alphai-Signature header matches the body.""" parts = dict(p.split("=", 1) for p in signature_header.split(",") if "=" in p) ts, sig = parts.get("t"), parts.get("v1") if not ts or not sig: return False # malformed header is a failed check, not an exception expected = hmac.new( secret.encode(), ts.encode() + b"." + body, hashlib.sha256, ).hexdigest() return hmac.compare_digest(expected, sig) # In your handler: # verify(os.environ["ALPHAI_WEBHOOK_SECRET"], request.headers["X-Alphai-Signature"], request.body)100%Website100%REST API100%Public API gate100%MCP serverThe probes run from GitHub Actions, outside our own infrastructure, so the status page stays reachable when our services are not. The API probe is a deep one and passes only when the database and the cache both answer. Response times, history and past incidents are public.FAQQuestions, answered.The short version of what the stock news API is, what the free tier gives you, and how it fits next to a market-data API.What is the alphai stock news API?A REST API that serves financial news as plain JSON over HTTPS. Every article arrives already scored for relevance (1–10) and tagged with the tickers it affects, plus per-ticker sentiment and written reasoning. Authenticate with a Bearer key, then filter by symbol, category, or minimum relevance and page the feed with a cursor. The same API powers alphai.io itself.Is there a free financial news API?Yes. The Free plan gives you one API key, capped at 20 requests a minute and 100 a day. That's enough to evaluate the feed and build a prototype, and it doesn't ask for a credit card. For production and commercial use, Basic and Pro raise the caps and open more of the archive.How is this different from a market-data or financial-data API?Market-data APIs give you prices, fundamentals, and OHLC bars. alphai is a news API. It tells you what happened, which tickers it touches, and how material it is, but it won't quote you a price. Many teams pair it with a market-data API and use the relevance score and sentiment to decide which stories a model or trading bot should act on.Does the API cover SEC filings and insider trading?Yes. SEC EDGAR Form 4 insider filings flow through the same feed as press news, in the same JSON shape. Query them with ?category=insider or the dedicated /api/news/insider/ endpoint, and pull a 30-day per-ticker rollup from /api/symbols/{ticker}/insider-summary/. 8-K filings are in there too, categorized by item: earnings releases under ?category=earnings, completed acquisitions under mergers_acquisitions, the rest under corporate_actions.Build on the beat.Sign up for any plan, generate a key in your account, and start shipping.Get API key

blocks.html_en: Articles reach the feed later than their publish time: general news lands a median of ~33 minutes after publication, SEC filings in 5 to 9 minutes (measured 2026-07-25). A poller that tracks time_published therefore misses late arrivals. sort=ingested returns rows in the order they entered the feed instead: call once without a cursor, store the next_cursor, then repeat the call with it. In this mode every response carries a cursor, and an empty results list means you are caught up. All filters work unchanged. Responses are cached for 60 seconds, so polling more often than once a minute buys nothing. Keep passing sort=ingested on every call: each mode issues its own cursors, and replaying one into the other mode returns a 400 rather than silently restarting at the top of the feed. 用于交易机器人的股票新闻 API。根据请求。

为 alphai 提供支持的同一提要，以纯 JSON 形式提供。 每篇文章都会根据相关性进行评分并链接到股票行情，因此交易机器人或代理后端可以在请求时过滤电汇。 Auth 是一个 Bearer 标头。

  -G -d "symbol=NVDA" -d "min_relevance=7"

Fresh

新文章在发表后一小时内登陆； SEC 文件在几分钟内就变成了 Feed 行（中位数约为 6 分钟）。 根据您自己的时间表轮询提要。

股票代码链接

文章带有机器提取的股票代码，每个股票代码都有自己的分析。

相关性评分

每篇文章都有法学硕士指定的相关性分数 (1-10)。 在请求时过滤。

SDK可选

通过 HTTPS 的纯 JSON。 带上任何 HTTP 客户端，或者安装官方类型化的 Python / TypeScript SDK（如果您愿意）。 无论哪种方式都没有锁定。

管道

数据来自哪里。

大多数财经新闻 API 都会给你一个消防水带并祝你好运。 我们会在故事向您发出请求之前进行过滤，因此到达 API 的部分是值得模型上下文窗口的部分。

01

收集

由 GDELT 驱动的监视器全天候监视全球金融新闻，而另一名工作人员则跟踪 SEC EDGAR 以提交表格 4 和 8-K。 出版商手工策划的 RSS 提要填补了双方都没有发现的空白。 所有内容都集中在一个 feed 中。

02

丰富

LLM 通过对每篇文章的相关性评分为 1-10 分，为其分配一个主题类别，并以置信度和推理来编写每个代码的情绪。

03

证实

提取的股票代码将根据活动交易品种列表和文章文本本身进行检查。 幻觉符号被丢弃，PR-wire 垃圾邮件域被彻底阻止，并且接近重复的符号被折叠成一排。

04

Serve

只有清除相关底线并至少携带一个经过验证的代码的文章才能到达 API。 从 6,900 多个受监控的源中，只有不到五分之一的人能够通过，因此噪音永远不会到达您的解析器。

不是嘲笑

现在，来自提要的真正的一行。

最新文章得分为 8 或更高，与 /api/news/ 返回的结果完全相同。 本页未涵盖的字段已根据长度进行了删减；形状才是真正的契约。

官方SDK

类型化的客户端，两种语言。

更喜欢打字客户端而不是手动请求？ 官方 Python 和 TypeScript SDK 包装了所有九个端点，并为您处理光标分页、429/5xx 重试、键入错误和速率限制检查。 它们采用相同的密钥并返回相同的数据，因此您可以稍后采用或永远不采用。

import hashlib
import hmac

def verify(secret: str, signature_header: str, body: bytes) -> bool:
    """Return True iff X-Alphai-Signature header matches the body."""
    parts = dict(p.split("=", 1) for p in signature_header.split(",") if "=" in p)
    ts, sig = parts.get("t"), parts.get("v1")
    if not ts or not sig:
        return False  # malformed header is a failed check, not an exception
    expected = hmac.new(
        secret.encode(),
        ts.encode() + b"." + body,
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected, sig)
